name: Vesuvius AD 79 - Plinian analogue
description: Scenario tuned to the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum. The eruption began with a sustained Plinian column (Pliny the Younger's eyewitness account) followed by repeated column collapses generating the pyroclastic density currents that killed the inhabitants of Herculaneum and Pompeii. VEI 5.
historical_note: PDCs reached Herculaneum (~7 km) within minutes; later surges reached Pompeii (~10 km). The low Heim coefficient reflects the high mobility of these flows.
